title: [MEDIUM] git-http-backend stderr and absolute server paths leak to remote client on backend errors
description:
**File:** [`crates/solid-pod-rs-git/src/service.rs`](https://github.com/DreamLab-AI/solid-pod-rs/blob/audit/git-disclosure/blob/audit/crates/solid-pod-rs-git/src/service.rs#L346-L542) (lines 346, 517, 527, 542)
**Project:** solid-pod-git-disclosure
**Severity:** MEDIUM  •  **Confidence:** medium  •  **Slug:** `secret-in-log`

## Owners

**Suggested assignee:** `noreply@anthropic.com` _(via last-committer)_

## Finding

When the CGI exits non-zero with empty stdout, spawn_cgi returns GitError::BackendFailed{stderr} with the raw captured stderr (lines 539-544; also the timeout branches 515-518/525-528). The auto-init failure path embeds the absolute server path repo_abs.display() into the error (line 346). error.rs's Display for BackendFailed interpolates `stderr` verbatim (error.rs line 38), and the in-repo server surfaces this straight to the remote client as JSON: `handle_git` does `builder.json({"error": e.to_string()})` on the 500 path (solid-pod-rs-server/src/lib.rs line 4837). A read whose CGI invocation fails therefore returns git-http-backend's diagnostic text — which can include internal filesystem paths, repo layout, and git version/configuration detail — to an unauthenticated-at-transport remote caller. This is reachable on the shipped server (reads reach the CGI) and worse for any library consumer that wires the write/auto-init path.

## Recommendation

Do not propagate raw CGI stderr or absolute filesystem paths to the client. Log the detail server-side (tracing) and return a generic opaque 500 body to the caller. Strip repo_abs.display() from the auto-init error surfaced outward.

title: [BUG] GitResponse::error builds JSON by unescaped string interpolation
description:
**File:** [`crates/solid-pod-rs-git/src/service.rs`](https://github.com/DreamLab-AI/solid-pod-rs/blob/audit/git-disclosure/blob/audit/crates/solid-pod-rs-git/src/service.rs#L170-L172) (lines 170, 172)
**Project:** solid-pod-git-disclosure
**Severity:** BUG  •  **Confidence:** high  •  **Slug:** `other-json-injection`

## Owners

**Suggested assignee:** `noreply@anthropic.com` _(via last-committer)_

## Finding

GitResponse::error formats the body as `format!("{{\"error\":\"{msg}\"}}")` (line 172) with content-type application/json. `msg` is caller-supplied and in practice derived from GitError variants that embed URL-controlled data (e.g. NotARepository(slug), PathTraversal(path)). A slug/path containing a double-quote, backslash, or control character produces malformed JSON and lets an attacker inject arbitrary content into the JSON `error` value. Not XSS (JSON content type) but a correctness/robustness defect and a minor response-injection vector for any binder using this helper. The in-repo server happens to use serde_json instead, but this is a public library helper.

## Recommendation

Build the body with serde_json::json!({"error": msg}).to_string() (or manual escaping) so the message is always correctly encoded.

title: [BUG] Substring-based is_write misclassifies reads of repos named like a service, and can auto-init on GET
description:
**File:** [`crates/solid-pod-rs-git/src/service.rs`](https://github.com/DreamLab-AI/solid-pod-rs/blob/audit/git-disclosure/blob/audit/crates/solid-pod-rs-git/src/service.rs#L129-L340) (lines 129, 144, 340)
**Project:** solid-pod-git-disclosure
**Severity:** BUG  •  **Confidence:** medium  •  **Slug:** `other-logic-bug`

## Owners

**Suggested assignee:** `noreply@anthropic.com` _(via last-committer)_

## Finding

is_write() uses `path.contains("/git-receive-pack")` and is_read() returns false whenever is_write() is true (lines 130, 144). A read request to a repo whose name contains the service string — e.g. GET /alice/git-receive-pack-notes/info/refs — is classified as a write. In a library deployment that installs an auth provider (so the write branch runs) and relies on the service's own gate, this GET is routed down the write path: it demands write auth, skips the push-path guard (which keys off the narrower ends_with("/git-receive-pack")), and if the repo's .git is missing it triggers on-demand auto-init (lines 338-350) — i.e. a GET creates a repository. The shipped server dodges this only because it refuses all writes upstream. Classifying repository data operations by unanchored substring match on the URL is fragile.

## Recommendation

Match the service verbs against the final path segment (strip query first, then check the last component equals/ends with the exact service name) rather than `contains`, and derive is_write/is_read from the same anchored parse the push guard uses.

title: [BUG] with_auth doc claims anonymous push without a provider, but the code fails closed
description:
**File:** [`crates/solid-pod-rs-git/src/service.rs`](https://github.com/DreamLab-AI/solid-pod-rs/blob/audit/git-disclosure/blob/audit/crates/solid-pod-rs-git/src/service.rs#L267-L318) (lines 267, 318)
**Project:** solid-pod-git-disclosure
**Severity:** BUG  •  **Confidence:** high  •  **Slug:** `other-doc-mismatch`

## Owners

**Suggested assignee:** `noreply@anthropic.com` _(via last-committer)_

## Finding

The with_auth doc (lines 267-269) states "Without one, write requests still succeed — the service becomes an anonymous-push setup". The actual code fails closed: for a write (or an auth-required read) with no provider configured, handle() returns GitError::Unauthorised("no auth provider configured") (lines 315-320). The documentation describes the opposite of the implemented security behaviour; a consumer trusting the doc could believe they must always install auth to prevent anonymous pushes, or mis-reason about the default posture.

## Recommendation

Correct the doc to state that writes (and auth-required reads) fail closed with 401 when no auth provider is configured.
